html:
The Yeke kingdom was a trading state in Katanga, in the south-east of what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo, built by the merchant Msiri from the 1850s until his death in 1891. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

Msiri was a Nyamwezi trader from what is now Tanzania. His followers, called Yeke, settled among the local people, and he made himself king at the expense of Kazembe and the Luba. From his capital at Bunkeya he sold copper, ivory and slaves to traders from both the east and the west coasts, and bought guns with them.

In the 1880s the agents of Leopold II and of Cecil Rhodes raced to win Katanga's copper. In 1891 an expedition for Leopold's Congo Free State reached Bunkeya, and one of its officers shot Msiri dead. Katanga became part of the Free State and later of the Belgian Congo, where its copper mines made fortunes.
